title: SQL Injection (login bypass)
impact: An attacker can bypass the login process without valid credentials and obtain full administrator access, exposing application data and administrative functions.
remediation: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements during authentication so that user input is processed as data and cannot alter the SQL query.

title: SQL Injection (data extraction via search)
payload_used: ')) UNION SELECT id, email, password, '4', '5', '6', '7', '8', '9' FROM Users--
impact: An attacker can retrieve confidential information from backend database tables without authorization, including email addresses, password hashes, and database structure details.
remediation: Use bound parameters in product search queries and enforce strict validation of search input.

title: Reflected XSS
impact: An attacker can run arbitrary JavaScript within a victim's browser session, potentially stealing session cookies, collecting login credentials, or redirecting the victim to harmful websites.
remediation: Encode user-provided search parameters according to their output context before displaying them in the DOM, and enforce a Content Security Policy (CSP).

title: Stored XSS
impact: Stored malicious scripts can execute repeatedly when users or administrators open saved feedback, potentially compromising administrator sessions and allowing unauthorized changes.
remediation: Clean user-submitted HTML with a trusted sanitization library such as DOMPurify before saving it, and apply HTML entity encoding when displaying the stored content.
